title: fleet throughput verification suite for dedicated capacity sign-off
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Build a reproducible verification suite ("throughput signature" tests + SLA sign-off) for Dedicated capacity customers. The suite will: 1) exercise autoscaling policies and fleet controls under controlled load; 2) produce deterministic, comparable throughput/latency profiles across hardware types and model variants; 3) provide artifacts required for customer acceptance testing (CAT) and contractual throughput guarantees. It is intended for use by platform engineers running pre-deployment verification, SRE-run periodic checks, and Solutions Engineers during customer onboarding sign-off.
background_and_rationale: Customers buying reserved GPU pools require measurable throughput guarantees. Current ad-hoc benchmarking is noisy and lacks standard traffic shapes, KV-cache scenarios, and long-tail stability checks. This ticket scopes a single verification suite that unifies: traffic generation, measurement collection, reproducible environment snapshots, and a sign-off report template. This reduces variance in acceptance decisions and speeds customer onboarding.
objectives: Define canonical traffic profiles (burst, steady-state, mixed with spikes) and sequence length distributions for LLM workloads
Implement a harness to drive RPCs against Dedicated endpoints (gRPC/HTTP) with token-accurate generation and KV-cache control
Measure and report throughput (tokens/sec), request/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, GPU/CPU utilization, and KV cache hit/miss stats
Validate autoscaling policies end-to-end: scale-up thresholds, cooldowns, scale-down behavior, and fleet rebalancing during maintenance/drain
Produce a Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) runbook and sign-off checklist with artifacts for contractual SLA verification
acceptance_criteria: Verification suite runs end-to-end in CI/test cluster and produces reproducible baseline report
Sustained throughput test: for each target config (model/quant/hw), tokens/sec is within 10% of baseline for 30 continuous minutes with error rate < 0.1%
Autoscaling validation: simulated increasing load triggers configured scale-up steps within the configured SLA window and scale-down does not cause request loss above threshold
Fleet control validation: draining an instance shifts traffic with <5% request rate imbalance and no request failures; weighted routing respects configured weights within 5%
Customer Acceptance Test playbook documented and validated by Solutions Engineering on one pilot customer run
test_plan: Traffic profiles: steady-1 (constant), burst (exponential ramps), mix (80/20 small/large seq), and cold-warm KV-cache toggles
Sequence length matrix: [16, 64, 256, 1024] tokens per request to cover common LLM patterns
Model variants: float32 baseline, int8 quantized, and trimmed/lite variants used for fallbacks
Hardware matrix: T4 (entry), A100 (standard), H100 (premium) — run identical jobs to collect comparators
Warm/cold KV cache scenarios: cold start (cache cleared), warm (prefilled with realistic prefix cache), and continuous streaming to exercise KV eviction
Duration and stability: sustained runs of 30m, 1h stress run, and a 12h overnight stability job for regression detection
Network conditions: optional packet loss and latency emulation to test regional fallbacks and graceful degradation
implementation_notes: Prototype driver using Locust for HTTP + custom gRPC client for token-accurate generation; switch to a single harness binary for production runs
Leverage the existing runtime benchmarking infra but isolate Dedicated pools using placard labels to avoid cross-tenant interference
Export metrics via Prometheus and aggregate with existing dashboards; store raw traces and payload captures in S3 for replayability
Provide a Docker image and k8s Job manifest for on-demand runs; add a small runner in the Console under the 'Dedicated' space for Solutions Engineers
Seed prompt sets and randomization must be recorded (seed value + prompt list) so runs are reproducible across clusters
Integrate with GitHub actions for nightly smoke and a separate perf CI lane for scheduled long runs
artifact_and_reporting_requirements: Signed-off PDF report including: environment snapshot, benchmark parameters, time-series graphs (throughput, p95/p99), GPU utilization heatmaps, and anomalies
CSV exports of raw measurement points and a replay bundle (prometheus snapshots + payloads) for audits
A machine-readable JSON summary for Console ingestion to show throughput guarantees on the customer account page
PR that includes the harness code, k8s manifests, and a sample CAT runbook used for the pilot customer
customer_acceptance_test_playbook: Preflight: collect customer model/version, requested throughput target, tokenization characteristics, and typical prompt distribution
Environment provisioning: create isolated Dedicated pool per the customer's commit (matching vCPU/GPU ratios and network egress configuration)
Baseline run: execute cold-start and warm-cache steady-state tests to generate baseline report
SLA validation: run the sustained throughput test and autoscaling exercise; compare collected metrics against contractual thresholds
Sign-off: deliver report, provide replay bundles, and obtain customer acknowledgement (email/Confluence note); if metrics fail, run mitigation steps (tuning batching/quantization/config) and re-run
Post-run: attach artifacts to the customer's account and create a follow-up task if remediation was required
risks_and_mitigations: Noise from co-located tenants: mitigate by using isolated Dedicated pools and ensuring network/host placement controls
Non-deterministic performance due to kernel scheduling: mitigate by pinning kernel versions and recording compilation artifacts
Large result objects causing measurement overhead: capture token accounting separately from payload transfer and measure token/sec at the runtime boundary
Customer data sensitivity: do not store customer prompts; use anonymized or synthetic prompt sets for public baselines and require customer opt-in for using real data
